In a statement issued Thursday, Nov. 19, GCC Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi expressed support for the UAE amid escalating diplomatic tensions between Mogadishu and Abu Dhabi. advertisements Albudaiwi criticized statements by officials of Somalia's federal government, accusing them of spreading allegations that undermine the UAE's regional and international role. The GCC statement described the remarks as irresponsible and denounced what it called malicious media campaigns directed against one of its member states. The secretary-general defended the UAE's diplomatic activities, saying the country had made significant contributions to regional security, stability and international dialogue. “The UAE’s recent hosting of Russian-Ukrainian talks demonstrates its commitment to regional and international peace and security. These unacceptable allegations seek to undermine our efforts to promote dialogue and cooperation,” he said. Albudaiwi said the allegations against the UAE risked undermining its efforts to promote regional and international cooperation. He emphasized that GCC member states remained committed to advancing peace, stability and prosperity and would reject campaigns intended to damage the reputation of any member state. “The GCC states remain steadfast in their approach to consolidating security, stability, and prosperity, and categorically reject any media campaigns aimed at offending any of their member states. Such campaigns will not affect the continuation of their role in supporting peace and security across the region and the world,” the statement added. The statement comes amid a sharp deterioration in diplomatic relations between Somalia and the UAE following accusations by President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud that Abu Dhabi has interfered in Somalia's domestic political and security affairs. In a televised address Tuesday, Hassan Sheikh accused the UAE of providing political, financial and security support to regional administrations and armed groups operating outside the federal government's control. He also criticized Emirati agreements involving the ports of Berbera, Bosaso and Kismayo, arguing that such arrangements undermine Somalia's sovereignty and should be negotiated through Mogadishu. On Thursday, Somalia's Cabinet ordered the UAE ambassador to leave the country within 72 hours and recalled its ambassador from Abu Dhabi for consultations. The Somali government said the measures were intended to protect its sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity. The UAE Foreign Ministry responded by condemning what it described as the Somali government's hostile approach, accusing Mogadishu of allowing internal political disputes to damage bilateral relations. Abu Dhabi also said it had closed its embassy in Mogadishu and withdrawn its diplomatic personnel in January 2026, following earlier disagreements over Somalia's cancellation of bilateral agreements. The GCC's latest statement adds a regional dimension to the dispute, with the six-member Gulf bloc publicly defending the UAE against Somalia's accusations. The GCC comprises the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman. The council did not announce any diplomatic or economic measures against Somalia, limiting its response to a public condemnation of the Somali government's statements and expressions of support for the UAE. somalia.content: Somalia Is Not for Sale — A United People Stand Behind Their Government in Defence of National Sovereignty - Hiiraan Online Jobs | Twitter | Somali Links | RSS Dark Mode Hiiraan Online HOME OPINION POLITICS RSS CONTACT US FACEBOOK × OPINION WARARKA MAANTA SPORTS SECURITY POLITICS Privacy Policy Contact Us Jobs advertisements HOME OPINION Somalia Is Not for Sale — A United People Stand Behind Their Government in Defence of National Sovereignty Share Facebook Messenger Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Copy Link Email Font Size A- A A+ By Ridwan Yusuf Mohamud Founder and Editor in Chief of Somali Magazine Saturday November 21, 2026 There are moments in a nation’s history when its people must look beyond political differences, regional affiliations and clan divisions to defend something greater than themselves: their country’s sovereignty, independence and national dignity. Somalia is facing such a moment. As diplomatic tensions between Somalia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) intensify, the position taken by the Federal Government has placed an important national question at the centre of public debate: who has the right to determine Somalia’s future? The answer should be clear. It is the Somali people, through their legitimate national institutions and constitutional processes. The Federal Government’s decision to take diplomatic action against the UAE reflects the seriousness of the disagreement over Somalia’s sovereignty and internal affairs. This is not merely a disagreement between two governments. It touches on the fundamental principles of national independence, territorial integrity and the authority of the Somali state. This Is Bigger Than Politics For decades, Somalia has paid a heavy price for internal divisions, political rivalries and external involvement in its affairs. The consequences have been felt by generations of Somalis, from Mogadishu to the regions and across the diaspora. Today, the country cannot afford to allow political disagreements to undermine its national interests. Somalis have every right to disagree with their government, question its decisions and demand accountability. That is part of responsible citizenship. However, when the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity are at stake, national interests must take precedence over political differences. Standing behind the government’s defence of national sovereignty does not mean giving political leaders a blank cheque. It means recognising that the independence of the Somali state must be protected regardless of who occupies the presidential office. Foreign Partnerships Must Respect Somalia Somalia welcomes international investment, trade, development assistance and security cooperation. The UAE, like other international partners, can play a role in Somalia’s economic development. However, cooperation must be based on mutual respect and recognition of Somalia’s national institutions. No foreign government should be in a position to determine Somalia’s political direction or undermine its territorial integrity. Strategic agreements and security arrangements affecting the country must respect its constitutional framework and national authority. Diplomatic disagreements should be addressed through dialogue, international law and peaceful engagement, but sovereignty must remain the guiding principle. Somalia should never have to compromise its national independence in exchange for investment, financial assistance or diplomatic relationships. Genuine partnerships strengthen nations; they do not weaken their institutions or challenge their territorial integrity. A Message to the Somali People This is a moment for Somalis everywhere to reflect on the kind of country they want to build. A country that speaks with dignity internationally, protects its national interests, strengthens its institutions and makes decisions independently. Political leaders must also recognise that national unity requires responsibility, transparency and inclusive leadership. The government has a duty to protect the country, but it must equally earn public confidence through accountable governance. The Somali people should not allow their differences to become opportunities for external interests to influence the country’s future. From Mogadishu to Hargeisa, Garowe, Kismayo, Baidoa and the Somali diaspora, the principle of national sovereignty deserves serious consideration and collective commitment. The current diplomatic situation should also remind Somali political leaders that the country’s national interests must never become secondary to personal ambitions, regional rivalries or political calculations. Somalia needs a united national position, strong institutions and leadership capable of representing the entire country. Somalia Must Come First The strength of a nation is not measured only by its military capabilities, economic resources or diplomatic relationships. It is also measured by the willingness of its people to defend their independence and stand together when their national interests are challenged. Somalia has endured too much to allow another generation to inherit a divided country. This is not about hostility towards the Emirati people. It is about respect between nations and the fundamental right of Somalia to govern its own affairs. The UAE and Somalia may have a history of economic, diplomatic and security cooperation, but no relationship should come at the expense of Somalia’s sovereignty. Friendship between nations must be built on equality, mutual respect and respect for national institutions. The Somali people must understand that defending their country is not the responsibility of the president alone, nor is it the responsibility of one political party, one region or one community. It is a collective national responsibility. The Somali people may disagree on politics, leadership and government policies, but they should never disagree on the fundamental right of their country to exist as a sovereign and independent nation. This is the time to put Somalia first. To stand above clan divisions, political rivalries and regional differences. To defend the country’s independence while demanding accountable leadership and responsible governance. Somalia belongs to its people. Its sovereignty is not for sale, its territorial integrity is not negotiable, and its future must be determined by Somalis themselves. One nation. One sovereignty. One future. somalia.summary: The Swedish Equality Ombudsman (DO) has filed a lawsuit against the Swedish Police regarding the killing of Mohamed, a 14-year-old Somali boy, in July 2023. The case, set for hearings on May 13, 14, and 27, 2027, will determine if Mohamed's family faced discrimination due to their ethnic background and if they are entitled to 300,000 Swedish kronor in compensation. Mohamed went missing from a care facility, and despite his family's warnings about his safety, police failed to act, leading to his abduction and murder by members of an organized crime network. The DO claims the police did not provide an interpreter for Mohamed's mother and did not follow up as promised. Although the police admitted to violating administrative law and the Convention on the Rights of the Child in 2025, they denied any discrimination. This case marks the first discrimination lawsuit the DO has brought against the Swedish Police, raising concerns about their treatment of immigrant families.

In a formal statement issued on November 15 and updated on November 17, the monitoring group stated that Somaliland authorities carried out the executions following presidential authorization without releasing full trial judgments, evidentiary findings, or appeal records for any of the nine men. According to information received by the organization, Ahmed’s immediate family was also not notified prior to his execution. Contradictions in Official Erigavo Records According to SHRMG, Ahmed was participating in a government-ordered security deployment in Erigavo, the regional capital of Sanaag, in May 2024 when an 18-year-old resident, Ayaanle Maxamuud Cumar, was fatally shot. The organization reported that Ahmed had no prior personal relationship with the deceased and caused the death accidentally while acting under official instructions. To substantiate concerns over institutional accountability, the group published three official government letters spanning 2024 and 2025 concerning Cumar’s death. The first letter, issued by the Somaliland Police Force on May 28, 2024, under reference KT/TCB/3/3-24/2024, recorded that Sanaag regional police fatally shot Cumar on May 16, 2024, during security preparations for the May 18 commemorations, and formally requested state compensation for his family. Subsequent ministerial correspondence reinforced that account. On June 29, 2024, then-Interior Minister Mohamed Kaahin Ahmed forwarded the police compensation request to the presidency under reference WAG/XW/412/831/482/06/2024, recommending state payment because the fatality occurred during a government security operation. On April 15, 2025, Minister of Interior and Security Cabdalle Maxamed Carab reiterated the recommendation to the president under reference WAG/AM/XW/121/18/2025. SHRMG noted that while the leaked letters do not independently establish whether compensation was paid or clarify the exact forensic link between the Sanaag regional police account and Ahmed’s prosecution, they demonstrate that authorities formally recognized the shooting as an operational incident warranting state restitution long before executing Ahmed. International Legal Standards and Qisas Claims The rights group argued that executing a defendant for an unintentional or negligent killing during a state mission violates Article 6 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), alongside UN Human Rights Committee General Comment No. 36, which restricts capital punishment strictly to crimes involving intentional killing. The statement also cited fair-trial guarantees under Article 14 of the ICCPR and the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights. While Somaliland authorities have reportedly justified the November 11 executions under the Islamic legal principle of Qisas, SHRMG maintained that invoking religious jurisprudence does not absolve judicial institutions from proving criminal intent, ensuring transparent trials, or verifying whether victims’ families were freely offered the option of blood compensation, known as diya, without coercion. The monitoring group issued ten demands to Hargeisa, calling for the immediate publication of Ahmed’s complete court file, disclosure of operational orders from the May 2024 Erigavo deployment, an independent inquiry into all nine executions, and an immediate moratorium on capital punishment. It also appealed to foreign embassies, UN Special Rapporteurs, and the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights to scrutinize the cases. Broader Scrutiny of Capital Punishment The November 11 deaths marked the second round of executions under President Cirro , following earlier firing-squad executions carried out at Mandera prison in previous years, as FTL Somalia previously reported . Meanwhile, security governance in the wider Sanaag region remains volatile amid overlapping territorial claims and unresolved local disputes, conditions highlighted during recent deadly Sanaag clan conflicts . The Mandera firing-squad executions also took place just days before Mogadishu voted in favor of a global suspension of capital punishment at the United Nations, a diplomatic move examined when Somalia backed a UN moratorium on executions despite continuing to impose death sentences domestically. Barely 48 hours after that New York vote, federal military courts underscored the domestic reliance on capital punishment when Somalia sentenced a NISA soldier to death for murder. FTL Critical Note The documentary record compiled by SHRMG exposes troubling opacity inside Somaliland’s judicial and security apparatus. When police command and two successive interior ministers formally document a fatal shooting as a state-directed security operation warranting government compensation, yet authorities subsequently execute an operative without releasing court judgments or notifying his family, public confidence in due process erodes. This lack of institutional transparency sits uneasily alongside Hargeisa’s sustained diplomatic campaign to present itself to Western capitals and international partners as a stable, rights-respecting democracy worthy of formal statehood recognition. Shielding military and criminal proceedings behind official silence while carrying out irreversible punishments undermines both domestic accountability and Somaliland’s broader claims to rule-of-law governance. somalia.summary: The Somaliland Human Rights Monitoring Group (SHRMG) has called for an investigation into the recent execution of Akram Buraale Ahmed and eight others at Mandera prison on November 11, 2026. The group condemned the executions, which were authorized by the president without full trial records or family notifications. Ahmed was reportedly involved in a government security operation in Erigavo in May 2024, during which an accidental shooting resulted in the death of an 18-year-old. SHRMG highlighted inconsistencies in official records regarding the incident and argued that executing someone for unintentional killing violates international legal standards. They demanded the publication of court files, operational orders, and an independent inquiry into the executions, alongside a moratorium on capital punishment. This incident raises concerns about judicial transparency and accountability in Somaliland, especially as it seeks recognition as a stable democracy while continuing to impose death sentences.

football.content: أزمة الدوري السوداني.. المريخ يتسلم الحيثيات ويستعد لـ"كاس" أزمة الدوري السوداني.. المريخ يتسلم الحيثيات ويستعد لـ"كاس" مباريات اليوم رياضات كرة القدم الأخبار فيديو البطولات البرامج دول أزمة الدوري السوداني.. المريخ يتسلم الحيثيات ويستعد لـ"كاس" من مباراة سابقة بين عملاقي الكرة السودانية المريخ والهلال (winwin) 20 نوفمبر 2026 أزمة الدوري السوداني.. المريخ يتسلم الحيثيات ويستعد لـ"كاس" الهلال السوداني المريخ الدوري السوداني الممتاز كرة قدم حافظ محمد أحمد الخرطوم winwin أضفنا الى 'غوغل' تسلّم نادي المريخ السوداني، اليوم الجمعة 20 نوفمبر/ تشرين الثاني، الحيثيات التي استندت إليها لجنة الاستئنافات باتحاد كرة القدم السوداني في قرارها القاضي بالتراجع عن حكمها السابق، وتجريد الفريق من لقب النسخة الماضية للدوري الممتاز. وعكفت اللجنة القانونية بالنادي على دراسة هذه الحيثيات التي أعادت اللقب إلى نادي الهلال ، بعد أن كانت اللجنة قد قبلت في وقت سابق طعن المريخ وقررت منحه اللقب، وهو ما أثار ردود أفعال واسعة. المريخ يستعد لجولة جديدة بمحكمة التحكيم الرياضي وتستعد إدارة النادي من خلال فريقها القانوني لإعداد مذكرة وافية لرفعها إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية "كاس" خلال الفترة القليلة القادمة، عقب الانتهاء من تقييم حيثيات قرار لجنة الاستئنافات. وتأتي هذه الخطوة استمرارًا لضغط إدارة الرئيس مجاهد سهل على اتحاد كرة القدم ، وتشديد الخناق عليه في حالة كسبه للقضية عبر محكمة التحكيم الرياضي. اقرأ أيضًا مدرب الهلال السوداني يترقب 3 تحديات شاقة في مواجهة الشرطة! الهلال السوداني يتلقى دعما مزدوجا وزينباور يضع حدا للشائعات وتسعى إدارة المريخ لاستعادة لقب الدوري عبر محكمة التحكيم الرياضية "كاس"، في محاولة لتكرار سيناريو عام 2017؛ حين شهدت الكرة السودانية سابقة تاريخية بتتويج الفريق بقرار قضائي إثر شكوى أثارت جدلًا واسعًا، وانتهت بتجريد الغريم التقليدي الهلال من لقب كان قد أحرزه ميدانيًا، ليُمنح للمريخ في خطوة اعتبرت درسًا في الدفاع عن الحقوق عبر المسارات القانونية الدولية. يُذكر أنّ صراعًا قانونيًا محتدمًا نشب بين قطبي الكرة السودانية، عقب طعن المريخ في قانونية مشاركة عدد من محترفي الهلال في مباراة الديربي التي جمعت الفريقين في ختام الموسم. ورغم أنّ لجنة الاستئنافات حسمت القضية لصالح المريخ أولًا، عادت وقبلت طلب الفحص الذي قدمه الهلال لتعيد اللقب إليه مجددًا، مما دفع إدارة المريخ للتصعيد واللجوء إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية. النشرة البريدية اشترك معنا بالنشرة البريدية لتصلك آخر أخبار الرياضة اشترك معنا دول كرة القدم الأخبار الدوريات الفرق رياضات التنس كرة السلة رياضات ميكانيكية مبارايات اليوم الأخبار البرامج الفيديو عن الموقع تواصل معنا أعلن معنا وظائف سياسة الخصوصية الشروط والأحكام الملكية الفكرية خريطة الموقع winwin© جميع الحقوق محفوظة 2026 الشروط والأحكام | سياسة الخصوصية مباريات اليوم
football.summary: تسلم نادي المريخ السوداني، في 20 نوفمبر 2026، الحيثيات التي استندت إليها لجنة الاستئنافات باتحاد كرة القدم السوداني في قرارها بإعادة لقب الدوري الممتاز لنادي الهلال، بعد أن كان قد مُنح سابقًا للمريخ. وقد أثار هذا القرار ردود أفعال واسعة، حيث كانت اللجنة قد قبلت في البداية طعن المريخ. الآن، يستعد المريخ لتقديم مذكرة إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية "كاس" بعد تقييم الحيثيات، في خطوة تهدف لاستعادة اللقب. يأتي ذلك في إطار الضغط المستمر من إدارة النادي على اتحاد كرة القدم، مستندة إلى تجربة سابقة في 2017 حيث تم منح المريخ اللقب عبر قرار قضائي. الصراع القانوني بين المريخ والهلال يتصاعد، خاصة بعد الطعن في قانونية مشاركة بعض لاعبي الهلال في مباراة الديربي.
